task: Implement the minimum executable ED-Finder V3 Svelte/Babylon application baseline on the existing #601 branch migration/svelte-go-live-candidate. This is foundation work only; do NOT design or port Finder/Inspect yet. Start by reading CLAUDE.md, docs/development/v3-application-stack-decision.md, docs/development/v3-browser-validation-lanes.md, docs/colonisation-redesign/spatial-platform-architecture-decision.md, and the current apps/web foundation. Preserve the renderer-neutral Stage 27 boundaries: Svelte/SvelteKit owns application/domain orchestration and accessible DOM UI; Babylon owns only spatial/GPU runtime; domain/feature code must not import Babylon types. Requirements: (1) add the modular Babylon 9-class dependencies needed by apps/web, preferring @babylonjs/core-style packages, and update pnpm-lock.yaml using pnpm rather than hand editing; no monolithic babylonjs package. (2) Establish a small renderer-neutral spatial contract/host API under apps/web/src/lib/spatial (or a clearly equivalent location) that exposes lifecycle/state/events without Babylon types leaking outward. Reuse/adapt existing renderer-neutral SpatialSceneContract concepts where appropriate rather than inventing a competing domain model. (3) Implement a minimal Babylon runtime adapter behind that boundary with clean create/start/resize/dispose lifecycle. Prefer WebGPU when genuinely available, with a deterministic WebGL2 fallback; failure must surface as a bounded application/runtime status rather than an uncaught exception. Do not introduce arbitrary worldScale truth. (4) Implement a Svelte canvas host component using onMount/cleanup and ResizeObserver. It must be safe across navigation/remounts, dispose GPU resources/listeners correctly, and expose an accessible DOM status outside the canvas. (5) Give the existing V3 app a deliberately NON-PRODUCT spatial foundation surface that Cypress can visit (a dedicated foundation route or equivalently isolated surface is fine). It should render only minimal deterministic diagnostic geometry/background needed to prove the runtime; do not make aesthetic/product decisions for the fresh map and do not copy React/R3F visuals. Label it clearly as foundation/test scaffolding. (6) Add targeted unit/contract tests that enforce no Babylon imports in domain/feature-facing contracts and verify lifecycle semantics where practical. (7) Extend apps/web Cypress to prove the real Svelte/Babylon surface boots in Chrome and Firefox under the existing Product E2E workflow: canvas present, renderer-ready status, stable resize/remount/navigation behaviour, no uncaught runtime failure; capture a deterministic screenshot as evidence but do not establish the old React map as a visual baseline. Do not add Review Lab synthetic scenarios in this packet. (8) Keep normal E2E separate from Review Lab exactly as docs/development/v3-browser-validation-lanes.md requires. Do not make cypress-parity.yml invoke Review Lab machinery. (9) Update the relevant V3 docs/tests so they describe an executable Svelte+Babylon baseline accurately, including that the fresh map design still comes later. Do not claim Finder/Inspect is implemented. (10) Run the proportionate apps/web checks: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile after lock generation as appropriate, svelte check/type check, lint/format check, Vitest, production build, and Cypress for the new foundation surface if the worker environment supports the browser. Also run the repository unit/contract tests affected by your changes. Preserve #601's current consolidation work and do not overwrite newer branch edits. No production/Contabo access, no deployment, no DB/schema changes, no React map port, no Review Lab re-baseline in this packet. End with an exact files-changed summary, tests run/results, and any genuine blocker.
